conviction_note: The findings sum to slightly positive (+0.2). Easy Aug-Oct 2025 comps make a revenue beat and a strong October number likely, and the unchanged FY gross-margin guide implies a conservative Q4. Against that, opex has been raised at each of the last two prints. The scaled number is slightly negative (p_up 48 on a 10-point move) because the stock has sold 6 of its last 7 prints, including the last one, which had a beat and a +18% July acceleration but a raised marketing and G&A guide. The two numbers disagree on purpose: the reaction function overrules the fundamental read.
bar: Q3 2026 net sales consensus about $344.9M (+16.7% y/y on $295.6M): Benzinga $344.9M, MarketBeat $344.96M (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-3-revolve-group-inc-stock/), TheRightTrader $344.8M on 8 estimates. EPS $0.21 (EarningsWhispers, whisper $0.24; https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/RVLV/21618) to $0.2232 (MarketBeat). The company gives no revenue guide. Its Q3 guide (Q2 prepared remarks, https://s203.q4cdn.com/458606031/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/transcript/REVOLVE-Q2-2026-Management-Prepared-Remarks.pdf): gross margin 53.5-54.0% (down about 88bp y/y), fulfillment about 3.4%, selling and distribution about 17.5%, marketing about 15%, G&A about $43.5M, tax 24-26%. At $345M that guide works out to about $0.21-0.22 EPS (my arithmetic), so the EPS consensus sits on the guide. The company has beaten EPS consensus 7 quarters in a row. Several sources agree on the revenue bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,070,693 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, down from 5,083,491 at 2026-07-31, 6.84 days to cover (https://equibles.com/stocks/rvlv/short-interest). That is 5.7% of the 71.09M total shares, or about 9.8% of the roughly 41.7M Class A shares, which I back out of William Blair's 13G (2,333,717 shares = 5.6%; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746618/000164495626000026/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml). Moderate, not crowded, and covering into the print. The baseline has no 25-delta skew (null). The front-expiry put/call open-interest ratio is a strange 37.84 on 6,680 total contracts, so nearly all open interest is puts, possibly one block; direction unknown. Event-implied move 12.03%, ATM IV 78.8%. Stock $22.02: down 16.5% from $26.37 before the Q2 print, -2.65% over 5 days, +3.82% over 20 days, 30% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: Q3 comp arithmetic points to revenue above the $345M bar. July 2026 grew about 18% against July 2025 at +7% (two-year stack about 25%). Q3 2025 grew only 4% in total, so Aug-Sep 2025 grew roughly 2-3%. If the two-year stack holds, Aug-Sep 2026 grows about 20-22% and Q3 lands near +19-20% (about $352-355M), against a consensus of +16.7% ($344.9M) that assumes July fades.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not paid on this name. Q2 2026 revenue beat ($347.4M vs about $342M) plus the July +18% disclosure: -4.06% (StockStory: down more than 5% on the day). Q1 2026 +16% beat: -13.87%. Q3 2025: +11.01%, but on a margin beat, not revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at +16.7% sits below July's +18% even though the August-September comparison is easier than July's (+2-3% vs +7%). If the street had modelled the two-year stack, revenue consensus would sit nearer $350-355M. EarningsWhispers' preview says consensus 'holds up with only modest fading through August and September'. The comp math is public, though, so part of it is in the bar.
findings.independence: July 2025 +7% and Q3 2025 +4% come from different documents (Q2 2025 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746618/000095017025103061/rvlv-ex99_1.htm; Q3 2025 release, https://s203.q4cdn.com/458606031/files/doc_earnings/2025/q3/earnings-result/Revolve_Group_Q3_2025_Earnings_Press_Release_vF.pdf). Demand-side support, a proxy: Aritzia US net revenue +60.3% for the quarter to 2026-08-30 (https://retail-insider.com/retail-insider/2026/10/aritzia-reports-q2-fiscal-2027-financial-results-net-revenue-up-44-1-to-1-17-billion/). Shares its comp reasoning with the October finding, but covers a different period.

findings.finding: The October 2026 quarter-to-date sales number, which the company discloses in every release, laps October 2025 at only 'mid-single-digit' growth (Q4 2025 overall +10%). So the October headline will probably be high-teens or better. November-December 2025 comps are much harder (about +12%), so a strong October flatters Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the quarter-to-date number. April 2026 at +14% (a slowdown from Q1's +16%), together with a gross-margin guide cut: -13.87%. July 2026 at +18% (a 6-point acceleration) still fell -4.06%, because opex guidance went up at the same time. Strong numbers on this line have not been bought; a slowdown was punished hard.
findings.why_not_priced: Q4 revenue consensus is not visible to me. A stock 16.5% below its pre-Q2 price with two downgrades in the past month does not look positioned for a +20% October. If the easy comp were priced, I would expect the stock to have held its August level. Against that, buy-side models will have the comp, and a strong October on an easy comp may be discounted.
findings.independence: The Q4 2025 +10% total comes from the Q4 2025 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746618/000119312526067027/rvlv-ex99_1.htm), a different document. The comp-stack reasoning is shared with the Q3 finding.

findings.finding: The unchanged FY2026 gross-margin guide of 53.5-54.0% (midpoint 53.75%) already includes Q2's refund-boosted 56.6%. With Q1 at 52.7% and Q3 at its 53.75% guide midpoint, it implies Q4 2026 gross margin of about 52.0%, against 53.3% in Q4 2025: down about 130bp y/y. That is a conservative-looking set-up for a raised FY margin guide if Q3 lands in range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Gross margin is the line that has moved this stock most. Q3 2025's 347bp margin expansion and record profitability: +11.01%. The Q1 2026 FY gross-margin guide cut (53.7-54.2 to 53.5-54.0): -13.87%.
findings.why_not_priced: The implied Q4 margin is not stated anywhere; it has to be backed out of four quarters (Q1 52.7%, Q2 56.6%, Q3 guide, FY guide). My arithmetic uses estimated Q3/Q4 revenue weights (Q3 about $345M, Q4 about $365M). Management also said the guide excludes $1.4M of further IEEPA refund claims and does not bake in further return-rate gains. If the market read the guide as conservative, the stock would not have drifted 16% lower. It could also mean management expects Q4 markdowns, which is the bear reading.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 gross margin of 53.3% from the Q4 2025 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746618/000119312526067027/rvlv-ex99_1.htm). Q1 2026 gross margin of 52.7% from the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746618/000119312526206442/rvlv-ex99_1.htm). This is inference from company documents, not a stated number.

findings.finding: Opex guidance has gone up at each of the last two prints and Q4 already carries more brand spend. FY G&A guide moved $161-164M, then $164-168M (Q1), then $170-172M (Q2). The marketing guide moved 15.3-15.8%, then 15.8-16.0% (Q2), with Q4 marketing 'north of 16%' for 'key brand building investments'. Since then the company has opened the Aventura store (2026-09-29), named Dwyane Wade chief performance officer of Revolve Man and FWRD Man, and is receiving a 'much larger' Grow-Good restock. A third raise, or a 2027 investment-year message, is the base case on this line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue and EPS beat and July +18%, but marketing and G&A guides were raised; stock -4.06% to -5%. Q1 2026: G&A guide raised and gross-margin guide cut; -13.87%. Opex creep has been punished on both prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.21-0.22 matches the Q3 opex guide exactly, so it holds no buffer for further spending. Q4 and FY2027 estimates are not visible to me. The 16.5% fall since August may already carry some of this fear, which is why the size is below the median reaction.
findings.independence: Q2 raises from the Q2 prepared remarks (https://s203.q4cdn.com/458606031/files/doc_earnings/2026/q2/transcript/REVOLVE-Q2-2026-Management-Prepared-Remarks.pdf). New spending items: Aventura store and Wade appointment (https://fashionunited.com/news/retail/revolve-expands-retail-presence-with-first-florida-location-at-aventura-mall/2026102675370, 2026-10-26).

findings.finding: Payment-card data breach. The 8-K (Item 8.01, not 1.05) was filed 2026-10-30. Per state AG notices, access began around 2026-09-11, was discovered 2026-09-29 and customers were notified from 2026-10-29. The 179k 'headline' is only the sum of four states: Texas 127,200, Massachusetts 46,813, Iowa 3,918, Vermont 1,328. California, Revolve's largest market, has an undisclosed count, so the true total is probably far larger. The company says it expects no material impact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior breach. The stock fell -2.86% on 2026-10-30 and -1.92% on 2026-11-02 after the disclosure, so part of this is in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage repeats the 179k figure. Texas and Massachusetts counts that large imply something nearer a million-plus saved-card accounts, which raises remediation and class-action cost and a possible effect on Q4 conversion (customers re-entering cards). The call is where scope and cost get asked. This is a one-off with no stated path to the guide, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: State counts from a different source (https://www.claimdepot.com/data-breach/revolve-2026; https://therecord.media/resolve-fashion-retailer-data-breach-payment-cards, 2026-10-30). The scope extrapolation is my inference.

findings.finding: Short interest fell 20% into the print, from 5.08M shares (2026-07-31) to 4.07M (2026-10-15), with 6.84 days to cover and about 9.8% of Class A shares. Front-expiry open interest is almost all puts (put/call OI 37.84 on 6,680 contracts), so any positive surprise meets a still-meaningful short base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, the one recent up print, rose +11.01% on a margin beat, consistent with covering on a positive surprise. No positioning-specific history in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not a fundamental fact; it acts on the size of the reaction. The put-heavy open interest may be a hedge, not a view.
findings.independence: The put/call open-interest ratio comes from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options, front expiry 2026-11-20), a different source.

findings.finding: The founders' regular selling stopped. EDGAR shows Form 4s from the co-CEOs and MMMK Development about monthly from January to June 2026 (01-28, 02-13, 03-04, 03-20, 04-13, 04-29, 06-09) and none since 2026-06-09.
findings.why_not_priced: Absence of a filing is rarely aggregated. The likely benign explanation is that a 10b5-1 plan ended, or a blackout from the breach discovery on 2026-09-29. Weak evidence, sized near zero.

findings.finding: Counterparty and peer read since the company last spoke is mildly positive for demand. Aritzia's quarter to 2026-08-30: US net revenue +60.3%, digital +67.7%, outlook raised (reported 2026-10-08). LVMH Q3 2026 (2026-10-12) says the US was 'buoyant' and grew even as Fashion & Leather Goods fell 5% organic on China, supportive for FWRD's US luxury business. Abercrombie (2026-08-26) was mixed: total comps flat, Hollister -3%, FY raised to about +5%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured link in the baseline between peer prints and RVLV's own reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public peer prints and proxies only. Aritzia's growth is mostly its own store expansion, so the transmission to Revolve is weak; filed small.
findings.independence: LVMH: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/lvmh-q3-organic-revenue-growth-slows-amid-china-downturn/2026101375147. ANF: https://fashionunited.com/news/business/abercrombie-fitch-raises-outlook-after-strong-q2-performance/2026082774284. All three are proxies.

findings.finding: Sell-side sentiment has drifted down into the print. Raymond James cut its target from $28 to $25 in mid-October (snippet only; page returned 403). AAII counts two downgrades and no upgrades in the month to 2026-11-02. The stock is down 16.5% from its $26.37 pre-Q2 price against a $30.08 average target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-print downgrades around Q1 2025 came before a -9.87% reaction. No clean pattern.
findings.why_not_priced: Downgrades are public and are part of why the stock is down. They may reflect checks (web traffic, card data) that I could not see. Two readings: the bar is lowered (positive) or there is real data behind it (negative). Sized small negative and near zero.
findings.independence: AAII, 2026-11-03: https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/553411-why-revolve-group-inc8217s-rvlv-stock-is-up-669 (2 downgrades, 0 upgrades). The analysts and dates behind those downgrades were not found.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew. The put-dominated open interest and a stock 16.5% below its pre-Q2 price with downgrades lean bearish, while my fundamental items lean mildly positive on revenue and margin set-up. The reaction history (1 up in 7) and the opex-creep pattern pull the scaled number slightly negative.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells revenue beats): Q3 revenue-comp finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4; October quarter-to-date finding cut from +1.0 to +0.6; print_vs_bar trimmed from +2.5 to +2.0.
Lesson 5 (documents beat inference): implied-Q4-gross-margin finding, which is my arithmetic across four documents with estimated revenue weights, cut from +0.8 to +0.6.
Lesson 2 (one-offs) and the partly-priced drop: data-breach finding cut from -0.5 to -0.4.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest of about 9.8% of Class A with 6.8 days to cover is moderate, not crowded, so the opex-creep negative keeps its -1.5.
Left standing: opex-creep, positioning, insider-absence, peer and sell-side findings; abs_move 10 and p_up 48 unchanged.
